slides.text:
Two more items that live outside `main`, like constants.

A **type alias** is a second name for a type that already exists. It does not create a new type: both names are the same type, and values move between them freely. Pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
name Score means u32
name Level means u32

Score, Level and u32 are one type

slides.text: Use an alias to say what a number is for, or to shorten a type you repeat. Aliases are written in PascalCase, and since an item is not a statement, one can be declared above or below `main`.

A `const` is pasted wherever it is used. A **static** is a single fixed place in memory: every use reads that same place, and it lives as long as the program runs.

It is written like a const, with the type required, in SCREAMING_CASE. Its value must be known before the program starts, so it is a literal or built from consts.
Statics that can change exist too, but they need `unsafe` and are out of scope here. In this course a static is read only, like a const.

exercises.title: A startup banner
exercises.guide: A static can start from a const, and a static can be read as often as needed.

chunks.guide: Declare the limit as a const first.
A static needs its type written out, and a const can feed it. A text literal is `&str`.

notes.text: One value in one place for the whole program.

chunks.text:
static APP_NAME: &str = "ingrain";
static SEATS: u32 = MAX_USERS * 3;

chunks.guide: Print the banner, the numbers, and sign off with the name again.

output.text:
== ingrain ==
users: 40
seats: 120
spare: 80
bye from ingrain
